goal_shape: Several options are on the table and one of them has to be chosen, deferred, or refused.
_note: Hand-written first. v0.1.0 had THREE decorative hats and a floor of 5 that let you defer having gathered nothing. v0.2.0 gave each exit its own requirements, which forced `coverage` to become per-terminal. v0.3.0 made YELLOW wait for the evidence, and made the exits AGENT-CHOSEN rather than drawn -- the die decides what work to do next, never what the answer is. v0.4.0 preserves the affordability of `commit`: without it the die spends the budget on repeats and prices the strongest exit out of reach. v0.5.0 makes the probe CONDITIONAL on the attack declaring a disputed fact. v0.6.0 makes YELLOW and BLACK per-option and requires MATCHED DEPTH: commit and drop need every option steelmanned and attacked. v0.7.0 adds a work floor: commit unlocks only after two rounds of evidence, where defer and drop may be reached on one. See references/findings.md.

cards.brief: The question, the options on the table, how reversible the choice is, and when it must be made.
What would make one option better, and how a tie is broken. Written BEFORE the options are examined.
Which option you already want, in one line, deliberately WITHOUT justification.
Observations bearing on the options. No interpretation, no ranking.
An option nobody put on the table, and why it was missed.
The strongest honest case FOR ONE option, against the criteria. Name the option in `option`; each play must take a different one.
The strongest honest case AGAINST ONE option, at the same depth as its steelman. Name the option; set `disputed_fact` if resolving something would change the answer, else null.
Resolve a disputed fact that the attack turned up. Costs 2: this hat spends real resources.

The option chosen, why, and when the choice gets revisited. Requires every option to have been steelmanned AND attacked, and at least two rounds of evidence -- you may DEFER or DROP on one, never commit.
Not yet: what specifically would change the answer, and by when. The one exit that does NOT need every option examined.
None of these are acceptable, and why. Requires every option to have been steelmanned AND attacked -- you may not refuse a field you have not examined.

conditions.why: You may not commit over an unresolved disputed fact. But not every attack raises one, and requiring a probe unconditionally made EXECUTE mandatory on the commit path for no reason.
